'''Michael E. Jung''' is a Professor of Chemistry in the Department of Chemistry and Biochemistry at the [[University of California at Los Angeles]].

Michael Jung was born May 14, 1947, in [[New Orleans]], [[Louisiana]].<ref>[http://www.chem.ucla.edu/~jung/CV.html UCLA, Department of Chemistry and Biochemistry]</ref>

==Early life and education==
Jung received a B.A. from [[Rice University]] in [[Houston]], [[Texas]], in 1969 and a Ph.D. from [[Columbia University]] in [[New York City]] in 1973 where he did research with [[Gilbert Stork]].

==Career==
[[Image:Oxetanocin A.svg|thumb|right|150px|Oxetanocin A]]
[[Image:Halomon3D.png|thumb|right|150px|[[Halomon]]]]
[[Image:Enzalutamide-01.svg|thumb|right|150px|[[Enzalutamide]]]]
Jung then obtained a NATO Postdoctoral Fellowship to work with [[Albert Eschenmoser]] at the [[Eidgenössische Technische Hochschule]] in [[Zürich]], [[Switzerland]]. In 1974, he joined the faculty at UCLA, where he has spent his career. In 1979 Jung was awarded a Sloan research fellowship.<ref>{{cite web |title=Past Fellows |url=https://sloan.org/past-fellows |website=sloan.org}}</ref>

Jung's research is focused on the development of new reactions for [[organic synthesis]], including the Jung "non-aldol aldol" protocol, an alternate method for obtaining [[aldol]] products without using the classical [[aldol reaction]].<ref>[http://www.chem.ucla.edu/dept/Organic/Jung_Brochure.html Research Interests], Organic Chemistry Faculty, UCLA</ref>  He has also developed chemical syntheses for a variety of [[natural product]]s with [[antitumor]] and [[Antiviral drug|antiviral]] properties including [[tedanolide]]s,<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Jung |first1=Michael E. |last2=Yoo |first2=Dongwon |title=Synthesis of the C1–C12 fragment of the tedanolides. Selective hydroboration–protonation of allylic alcohol approach |journal=Tetrahedron Letters |date=January 2008 |volume=49 |issue=5 |pages=816–819 |doi=10.1016/j.tetlet.2007.11.181}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Jung |first1=Michael E. |last2=Lee |first2=Christopher P. |title=Synthesis of a Fully Functionalized Protected C1−C11 Fragment for the Synthesis of the Tedanolides |journal=Organic Letters |date=February 2001 |volume=3 |issue=3 |pages=333–336 |doi=10.1021/ol000329p|pmid=11428007 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Jung |first1=Michael E |last2=Lee |first2=Christopher P |title=Use of the non-aldol aldol process in the synthesis of the C1–C11 fragment of the tedanolides: use of lactol ethers in place of tetrahydrofurans |journal=Tetrahedron Letters |date=December 2000 |volume=41 |issue=50 |pages=9719–9723 |doi=10.1016/s0040-4039(00)01726-3}}</ref> [[oxetanocin]],<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Jung |first1=Michael E. |last2=Nichols |first2=Christopher J. |title=Highly stereoselective synthesis of trans,trans-4-aryl-2,3-oxetanedimethanols: Preparation of oxetanocin a analogues |journal=Tetrahedron Letters |date=October 1996 |volume=37 |issue=43 |pages=7667–7670 |doi=10.1016/0040-4039(96)01720-0}}</ref> [[halomon]]s,<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Jung |first1=Michael E. |last2=Parker |first2=Michael H. |title=Synthesis of Several Naturally Occurring Polyhalogenated Monoterpenes of the Halomon Class1 |journal=The Journal of Organic Chemistry |date=1 October 1997 |volume=62 |issue=21 |pages=7094–7095 |doi=10.1021/jo971371+ |pmid=11671809 |issn=0022-3263}}</ref> and [[xestobergsterol]].<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Jung |first1=Michael E |last2=Johnson |first2=Ted W |title=First total synthesis of xestobergsterol A and active structural analogues of the xestobergsterols |journal=Tetrahedron |date=February 2001 |volume=57 |issue=8 |pages=1449–1481 |doi=10.1016/s0040-4020(00)01086-3}}</ref> Other research interests include the bridged [[Robinson annulation]] and the mixed [[Lewis acid]] [[Diels-Alder]] process.<ref>[http://www.chem.ucla.edu/~jung/research.html Current Research Interest], UCLA</ref>
[[File:Apalutamide.svg|thumb|Apalutamide]]
Jung's research group developed an [[Receptor antagonist|antagonist]] of the [[androgen receptor]] [[enzalutamide]], which is a pharmaceutical drug used for the treatment of hormone refractory [[prostate cancer]].<ref>"New Prostate Cancer Agent Class: Rational design leads to novel drug candidate, now in clinical trials", ''[[Chemical and Engineering News]]'', September 22, 2008, Volume 86, Number 38 pp. 84-87</ref><ref>[http://www.chemistry.ucla.edu/news/item?item%5fid=43116 UCLA Chemistry and Biochemistry]</ref> An analog of enzalutamide, [[apalutamide]], was also FDA approved.  

==Awards==
* 2022 IUPAC-Richter Prize
* 2016 [[Glenn T. Seaborg Medal]], UCLA<ref>{{cite web |title=UCLA Glenn T. Seaborg Symposium - Previous Recipients |url=http://www.seaborg.ucla.edu/previous_recipients.html |website=www.seaborg.ucla.edu}}</ref>
* 2016 Richard C. [[Tolman Award]], Southern California Section of the American Chemical Society<ref>{{cite web |title=2015 Michael E. Jung, UCLA |url=https://scalacs.org/?page_id=2745 |website=SCALACS |date=24 March 2016}}</ref>
* 2015 American Association for Cancer Research [[AACR Awards]] Team Science Award<ref>{{cite web |title=AACR Team Science Award |url=https://www.aacr.org/Research/Awards/PAGES/TEAM-SCIENCE-AWARD-___8470D6.ASPX |website=www.aacr.org}}</ref>
* 1995 American Chemical Society [[Arthur C. Cope Scholar Award]]<ref>{{cite web |title=Arthur C. Cope Scholar Awards |url=https://www.acs.org/content/acs/en/funding-and-awards/awards/national/bytopic/arthur-cope-scholar-award.html |website=American Chemical Society |language=en}}</ref>
